memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Then the land will enjoy its sabbath years all the time that it lies
desolate and you are in the country of your enemies; then the land will
rest and enjoy its sabbaths. All the time that it lies desolate, the land
will have the rest it did not have during the sabbaths you lived in it'"
- Lev 26:34-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a haunting and remarkable detail. During the years of exile, the
land would finally get the sabbath rest that Israel had denied it. For all
those years when they refused to let the land rest every seventh year, the
rest was, in a sense, owed. And now it would be repaid — all at once, while
the people were gone.

There is a sobering lesson buried here. The commands we ignore do not
simply disappear. Israel had skipped the sabbath years, thinking they were
getting ahead. But the debt was recorded, and eventually it came due.

Dear reader, we cannot cheat God's design without cost. We may skip rest,
override the rhythms He built into life, and push relentlessly ahead — and
for a while it may seem to work. But the body, the soul, the family, the
relationship with God: these keep an account. The rest we refuse to take
willingly often gets taken from us later, through breakdown or collapse.

The principle beneath the sabbath still stands as wisdom, even though the
specific national law was Israel's. God built us to need rest. Jesus
Himself withdrew to rest and pulled His weary disciples aside to do the
same (Mark 6:31).

Do not force life to collect its rest from you the hard way. Build in the
rest God designed, and trust Him with what you set down.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I skipping the rest God built into life, thinking I am getting
   ahead?
2. What might eventually "come due" if I keep pushing without pause?
3. How can I honour God's design for rest before it is forced upon me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for refusing the rest You designed. Teach me to build
healthy rhythms into my life and to trust You with the work I set down.
Amen.
